newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Maize, milling wheat end mixed on Hungary's BCE.
newsitem.headline: Maize, milling wheat end mixed on Hungary's BCE.

text.p: Maize and milling wheat futures on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) closed mixed on Wednesday, indicating that some prices have begun to consolidate following recent sharp falls, traders said.

"Maize seems to have finished its drastic fall," said Termin Broker's Robert Vajo, adding that "for March to July maturities, substantial deals could be concluded at current levels in the next few days and weeks."

March maize closed 10 forints up at 17,210 forints a tonne, while November dropped 1,660 forints to 18,240. November maize can now fall without limit following five days of consecutive drops at the 400-forints limit.
March milling wheat futures finished at 24,500 forints, up 200, while May fell 1,200 forints to 24,850.
All other milling wheat maturities except July will lose their downside limits on Friday, traders said, but added that they did not see a slump in prices.

"Deals are likely to be concluded below today's settlement prices but I do not expect thousands of forints falls," Vajo said, adding that longer maturity milling wheat prices were likely to consolidate while nearbys may continue the recent declining trend.

But short-term trends were difficult to predict as export prices were hardly calculable because this year's flour and wheat exports have not yet started, traders said. ($=170.09 Hungarian forints. Lot size 20,000 kgs for all contracts.) -- Denes Albert, Budapest newsroom +36 1 327 4040
